clue.text: French elite can become rich

indicators.note: letters that can become something else are free to be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: FR is the standard abbreviation for French
taken as written

explanation.surface: France's upper classes can grow wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich soil or land is productive and abundant in growth, the same sense as fertile ground.

clue.text: Vessel with ensign on

parts.note: an ensign is a national flag flown by a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship flying its national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large drinking container for wine or ale, a kind of vessel in the sense of a receptacle.

clue.text: Australian tennis player raises the roof!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Pat ..., the Australian who won the US Open twice
second meaning: a sloping beam that holds a roof up, taken literally

explanation.surface: An Aussie tennis star gets the crowd cheering wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises the roof' is the idiom for noisy celebration, but here it is read literally: the timber that holds a roof aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is one of the sloping timbers supporting a roof, so it literally lifts and carries the roof structure.

clue.text: Draw picture of frail American with a king in the gallery

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits within it, so the king goes inside the gallery

parts.note: someone frail is sickly
US is short for the United States, so American
the Tate is the famous London art gallery
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A sickly American artist sketches a king in an art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate something is to make a drawing or picture of it, as in illustrating a book.

clue.text: Student comes in days before the fairies

indicators.note: someone who comes in enters, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A pupil turns up in the days leading up to a fairy celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small mischievous folklore beings, close kin to fairies in legend and story.

clue.text: Steps that make holes in stockings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: portable climbing frames with rungs
second meaning: what a snagged thread does to hosiery, running down the leg

explanation.surface: Climbing a stepladder snags your tights.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in a stocking is a run, where a broken thread unravels in a vertical line; the verb means to cause one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepladders are also called steps, and to ladder tights is to tear them so a run appears.

clue.text: Lake with many boats, which help to find the way

definitions.text: which help to find the way
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a plural noun

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
with and and both mean together
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many
an ark is a boat, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: A lake crowded with boats helps sailors navigate.
explanation.definitionFit: Landmarks are prominent features such as towers or hills that travellers use to orient themselves and navigate.

clue.text: Fade out without hearing

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sound slowly vanishing for someone losing their hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deaf lacks the ability to hear sound, literally lacking that sense.

clue.text: Spread of pied mice causes widespread disease

indicators.note: things spread out are scattered about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Piebald mice multiplying and spreading a plague.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is an outbreak of illness affecting many people in a community at once.

clue.text: Some nail is mixed up in the pudding

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled together, so the letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stray nail has been stirred into the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse wheat flour boiled with milk into a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Ghastly new law covering 50% of fuel

indicators.note: something covering another wraps around it, so the outer word encloses the inner
a new version is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word means keeping just two of its letters, here the front pair

parts.note: the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A dreadful new law that taxes half your fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly and awful are synonyms, both meaning very bad or horrifying.

clue.text: Deliberate damage results from vehicle running over girl and a boy

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

parts.words: running over girl and a boy
parts.note: the setter's names for these letters are unclear; the fragment has to supply the rest of the word

explanation.surface: A van mowing down two children leaves a scene of destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN is clear, but no standard girl and boy give the remaining letters; this clue is loose and is best solved from the definition and crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandalism is the wilful destruction or defacement of property, which is damage done on purpose.

clue.text: Frees bearing with identical magic formula

parts.note: to free a lock is to unfasten it
E is east, a compass bearing
identical things are alike

explanation.surface: Releasing someone using the very same spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba's cave of treasure opens to the spoken password.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Ali Baba is the archetypal spell or password that unlocks a sealed door.

clue.text: Misery of loveless greeting

indicators.note: less means without, and love is the zero score in tennis, a round letter to drop

parts.note: a common word of greeting

explanation.surface: The sadness of being greeted coldly, without affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis, so it stands for the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is used loosely for any state of great suffering or torment, so it means misery.

clue.text: Simple church tunes heard from the comfortable seats

parts.note: simple things are not difficult
CH is the abbreviation for church
airs are melodies that are listened to

explanation.surface: Plain hymns sung while worshippers sit in plush pews.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy chairs are large upholstered armchairs designed for relaxing in comfort.

clue.text: Doubt about booking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a misgiving or qualm
second meaning: a table or room held in advance

explanation.surface: Having second thoughts over a hotel booking.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservation is both a misgiving held back and an advance arrangement securing a seat or room.

clue.text: Midgets' housekeeper, who sent Women's Institute crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: A tiny people's housekeeper drives a women's club mad.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale the heroine keeps house for the seven dwarfs in their forest cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Grimm tale and Disney film, the princess cooks and cleans for the seven dwarfs.

clue.text: Scout around in top 100 to find kind of guitar

indicators.note: one item placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read here as the letters A and I

indicators.note: turned around in every direction, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A Boy Scout hunts through the pop charts for a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top 100' looks like a music chart; it splits into A1 (top) and C (100).
explanation.definitionFit: An acoustic guitar is the hollow-bodied kind that makes sound without electric amplification.

clue.text: Foreign currency scattered in harbour causes a problem

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it

parts.note: a quay is a landing wharf in a harbour

indicators.note: scattered things are strewn about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Foreign banknotes strewn about the docks create a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a dilemma, a state of perplexity about what to do next.

clue.text: Politely try to win over European organisation using several likely youths initially

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
E is short for European

indicators.note: initially points to the opening of each word in the run before it

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Courteously wooing a European body that employs promising youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European organisation' reads as one unit like the EU, but only European is a piece; organisation starts the run of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting courteously means behaving with good manners, which is what doing something politely is.

clue.text: Take money from handkerchief for fruit

indicators.note: to take something from a word is to remove it

parts.note: a bandana is a large patterned handkerchief
d was the symbol for the old British penny

explanation.surface: Pinching coins from a hankie to buy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971, British pennies were written d, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with a yellow skin.

clue.text: Massage a thrombosis

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rub gently with the hand
second meaning: a sudden blockage of blood to the brain

explanation.surface: A massage therapist and a blood clot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke is to caress with the hand, and a stroke is a seizure caused by a clot cutting off blood to the brain.

clue.text: Knock tops off milk containers to make vases

indicators.note: knocking the tops off removes the leading letters of the word

parts.note: churns are large metal milk cans

explanation.surface: Smashing the tops off milk cans to turn them into flower vases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' is plural, so the first two letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are tall rounded ornamental vessels, close enough to vases in ordinary use.

clue.text: Second, we point to the skill of the lover

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
taken as written
E, east, is a point of the compass
taken as written
art is craft or skill

explanation.surface: A moment later, we indicate the talent of the beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a person someone loves romantically, a darling or beloved.

clue.text: Bird of prey found in valleys around Scottish golf course

indicators.note: what is found inside sits within the outer word, so the surrounding letters are stripped away

parts.note: Gleneagles is a famous golf resort in Perthshire, Scotland
glens are Scottish valleys

explanation.surface: A raptor spotted in the glens near a Scottish golf links.
explanation.walkthrough: The course name wraps the valleys around the bird: GLEN + EAGLE + S.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large powerful raptor with a hooked beak, hunting other animals.

clue.text: Part of enormous pantechnicon stuck on bridge

indicators.note: part of a phrase means a run of consecutive letters lifted from it

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A huge removal lorry wedged on a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantechnicon is a British word for a large furniture removal van.
explanation.definitionFit: To span a gap is to bridge it, and a span is also the arch of a bridge between supports.

clue.text: Walk on heather, causing crushing

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Hikers stomping across the moorland flatten the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Trampling means treading heavily on something so as to flatten or crush it underfoot.

clue.text: State in answer to charge that I'd mislaid a hose

parts.note: surface padding: sets the scene of someone excusing themselves

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, as a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A gardener's excuse when accused of losing a hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer to charge that' is just scene-setting; the letters hide in mislaid a hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the American northwest.

clue.text: Stick around! Money produces spice

indicators.note: something placed around another wraps it, so the outer word encloses the inner

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Stay put and the cash will buy you spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper powder made from dried chillies, used as a seasoning.

clue.text: Trap for headless chickens — nature is heartless

indicators.note: without its head, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: hens are chickens

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its central letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Catching panicking chickens, nature at its cruellest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless chickens' suggests panic; here it just removes the first letter of the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a snare, so to trap an animal or person.
